To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prevalence of nutrient inadequaties was high for key micronutrients, including thiamin, vitamin A, vitamin C, and riboflavan, and all adults in the city of Sao Paulo had excess sodium intakes.

the prevalence of nutrient inadequatcies in the city of Sao Paulo is high for some key micronutrients, and the adjustment for the within person variability presents lower prevalence of nutrient inadequecy due to removal of the within-person variability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to assess the prevalence of inadequacies in micronutrient intake in the Brazilian population, using the PC-SIDE software, which allows for an estimation of usual intake.
the development of methods for the estimation of nutrient intake distributions in large population samples and the estimation of prevalence of nutrient inadequaties.

the development of statistical methods for the analysis of repeated dietary intake data and the application of those methods to the estimation of usual intake distributions and prevalence of nutrient inadeq uacy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) 100% of the adult population in São Paulo has excess sodium intake, 2) 58% and 52% of the females and males, respectively, have inadequate intake of vitamin A, 3) 62% and 52%, respectively, of the females and the males have inadequate intake of Vitamin C, 4) 50% and 41% of the females, respectively, and males have inadequate intake for thiamine, 5) 19%
the majority of adults in São Paulo are not getting enough vitamins A, C, and B, and are getting too much sodium in their diet.
the majority of adult residents of São Paul had inadequate intake of key micronutrients and excess sodium intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the statistical innovations of the PC-SIDE method improved the precision of the prevalence estimates of the risk of inadequacy and excess of intake for the micronutrients studied.
the use of statistical methods that adjust for within-person variation can improve the accuracy of the estimates of nutrient inadequacies.
statistical methods for estimating usual intake, when available, are useful in assessing the prevalence of inadequate intake and excessive intake in a population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to improve the estimates of the prevalence of nutrient risk populations by adjusting for within-person variability in intake.
the prevalence of inadequacies for key micronutrients is high in São Paulo.
the prevalence of nutrient inadequatcy is underestimated when only one dietary recall is used to assess nutrient intake.
